question: What makes an event a 'black swan'?
answer: Three things, in Taleb's definition: it lies outside what past experience suggests is possible; it has an extreme impact; and afterwards we make up explanations that make it look predictable. Europeans believed all swans were white until black ones were seen in Australia.
move: If it was predictable only afterwards, it wasn't predicted.
simply: Everyone was sure all swans were white, because every swan they'd seen was white. Then someone saw a black one, and the rule was gone.
why: The events that shape lives and markets the most are the ones no model expected. Planning for being surprised beats pretending to predict.
source: Nassim Nicholas Taleb, The Black Swan, 2007
reference: Nassim Nicholas Taleb, The Black Swan (Random House, 2007), prologue
